mainTopic: רב נחמן's five cases that need a gift of all one's property, and what a gift of 'my property' includes
overview: This amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion. רב אשי tells רבינא that a slave is not freed when his master keeps some land, because such a document is not a full גט שחרור that cuts him off from his master. Then רבא quotes רב נחמן, who lists five cases where a special rule applies only if the owner writes away ALL of his property: שכיב מרע, a slave, a wife, sons, and מברחת. The גמרא brings the source for each of the five. It then rules that keeping back movable property counts as keeping something, except in the כתובה case, since a כתובה is collected only from land. אמימר adds that movable items written into the כתובה, if they still exist, do count. A new topic follows: what does a gift of 'my property' include? The גמרא shows that slaves, land, movable items, money and documents are all called 'נכסי', and brings the story of רב פפא's money and רבה בר יצחק's two kinds of שטרות. The amud ends as רב הונא adds a third kind of שטר, and the משנה he points to comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The real reason the slave is not freed
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי tells רבינא that the slave is not freed because the document is not a full גט that cuts him off from his master.
steps.simpleTranslation: He (רב אשי) said to him (רבינא): We teach this rule because the document is not a 'cutting-off' bill of release.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers רבינא and gives the true reason behind the rule that a slave is not freed when the master keeps back some land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is not that the slave himself was part of what the master kept back. A גט שחרור must cut the slave off from his master completely. A document that leaves the master holding some of his property is not a complete break, so it cannot free the slave.

keyTerms.meaning: Cutting off, a complete break (like כריתות in a גט)
A document of release (here, a slave's גט שחרור)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the reason is 'maybe he kept the slave too.' רב אשי says the reason is that the document is not a complete break.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רב אשי is answering רבינא, carrying on the discussion from just before this.

phrases.english: We – because it is not
a cutting-off document, we teach it.
phrases.notes: He means a document that fully cuts the slave off from his master, the way a real גט must.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנַן – מִשּׁוּם דְּלָאו כְּרוֹת גִּיטָּא מַתְנֵינַן לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier exchange between רבינא and רב אשי about the slave who received the master's property.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The slave is not freed because perhaps the master kept the slave as part of what he held back.
steps.terutzMaskana: The slave is not freed because a document that leaves something with the master is not a full, cutting-off גט שחרור.

steps.title: Five cases that need the whole estate
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes רב נחמן: in five cases a special rule applies only when the owner writes away all of his property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב נחמן: There are five cases where the rule does not apply until they write over all their property. They are: a dying person, his slave, his wife, his sons, and a woman who hides her property away (מברחת).
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic opens. רב נחמן lists five situations that share one condition: their special rule applies only when ALL the property is given away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case has its own special law, but the trigger is the same. The law kicks in only if the giver held back nothing. מברחת is a woman about to marry who writes her property over to someone else so her husband will not get it. The גמרא will now explain each case one by one.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who is dangerously ill, on his deathbed
A woman who 'smuggles away' her property before marriage so her husband won't get it

steps.whyThisMatters: This list organizes several different laws under one shared idea: giving away everything shows something special about the giver's intent.

phrases.english: Rava said that Rav Naḥman said:
Five – not until they write over all their property;
and these are they:
a person on his deathbed, his slave,
his wife, and his sons, a woman who hides away her property.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: חֲמִשָּׁה עַד שֶׁיִּכְתְּבוּ כָּל נִכְסֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement. It connects to the slave case just discussed, since the slave is one of the five.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In five cases (שכיב מרע, slave, wife, sons, מברחת) the special law applies only when all the property is written away.

steps.title: The source for the dying person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the source for the שכיב מרע case: a משנה says his gift stands only if he kept some land for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: A dying person – as we learned in a משנה: A dying person who wrote all his property to others and kept any amount of land – his gift stands. If he did not keep any amount of land – his gift does not stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining the list. It brings the משנה that is the source for the first case, the שכיב מרע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a sick man gives away everything, we assume he only meant it in case he dies. So if he gets better, the gift is cancelled. If he kept even a little land, he was not giving everything because of death, so the gift stays even if he recovers. The special rule applies only when he gave all.

keyTerms.meaning: He held back / kept for himself
Any amount of land, even a tiny bit

steps.confusionAlert: 'His gift does not stand' is talking about when he recovers. If he dies, the gift is fine.

phrases.english: A person on his deathbed – as we learned:
A person on his deathbed who wrote
all his property to others,
and he held back any amount of land –
his gift stands;
phrases.notes: Even if he gets better, the gift stays.

phrases.english: if he did not hold back any amount of land –
his gift does not stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first item on רב נחמן's list.
steps.raayaObject: That the שכיב מרע's special rule depends on giving away all his property
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה (146b): a שכיב מרע who kept any land, his gift stands; if not, it does not stand.

steps.title: The source for the slave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the source for the slave case: a משנה says a slave given all the property goes free, but not if the master kept any land.
steps.simpleTranslation: His slave – as we learned in a משנה: One who writes all his property to his slave – the slave goes free. If he kept any amount of land – the slave does not go free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second case on the list and brings the משנה about a master who writes his property to his slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving the slave everything includes the slave himself, so he goes free. If the master kept even a little land, the slave is not freed. As רב אשי explained in step 1, such a document is not a complete break. So the freedom comes only when all is given.

keyTerms.meaning: He goes out a free man

steps.whatToRemember: In both the שכיב מרע case and the slave case, holding back even a tiny piece of land changes the result. That is the shared idea behind רב נחמן's list.

phrases.english: His slave – as we learned:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in פאה 3:8, the same rule discussed in step 1.

phrases.english: One who writes all his property to his slave –
he has gone out a free man,
if he held back any amount of land –
he has not gone out a free man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second item on רב נחמן's list, after the שכיב מרע.
steps.raayaObject: That freeing a slave through a gift of property depends on giving away all the property
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה (פאה 3:8): one who writes all his property to his slave frees him; if he kept any land, the slave is not freed.

steps.title: Source for the wife case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings שמואל's rule that a man who writes all his property to his wife only makes her a manager of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wife case comes from what רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: if a man writes all his property to his wife, he has only made her a manager over it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the third of רב נחמן's five cases, a man who gives everything to his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל says that when a man writes all his property to his wife, we assume he did not mean to give it to her as a gift. He only meant to make her the manager of it. Based on רב נחמן, this applies only when he gave away everything; if he kept something for himself, it is a real gift.

keyTerms.meaning: A manager or caretaker of property who does not own it
One who writes away all of his property

phrases.aramaic: אִשְׁתּוֹ – דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: His wife: as רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל:
phrases.notes: This is the next case on רב נחמן's list of five from step 2.

phrases.english: One who writes all his property to his wife,
has made her only a manager.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִשְׁתּוֹ – דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of sources for רב נחמן's five cases, moving from the slave to the wife.
steps.raayaObject: The wife case in רב נחמן's list
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל: one who writes all his property to his wife makes her only a manager

steps.title: Source for the sons case
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says that if a man writes all his property to his sons and gives his wife some land, she loses her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sons case comes from a משנה: if a man writes all his property to his sons and writes even a little land to his wife, she loses her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the fourth case, a man who gives everything to his sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By agreeing to take a small piece of land alongside the sons, the wife shows she accepts the split and gives up her כתובה. According to רב נחמן, this happens only when the husband gave away all his property. If he kept some land for himself, she does not lose her כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: Any amount of land, even a tiny bit
The marriage contract money owed to a wife if her husband dies or divorces her

phrases.english: His sons: as we learned in a משנה:
One who writes all his property to his sons,
and wrote any amount of land to his wife,
she has lost her כתובה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next case on the list, after the wife.
steps.raayaObject: The sons case in רב נחמן's list
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in פאה: writing all property to sons plus land to the wife makes her lose her כתובה

steps.title: Source for the woman sheltering her property
steps.stepSummary: A woman who wants to keep her property away from her future husband must write away all of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case of the woman who shelters her property comes from what the master said: such a woman must write away all of her property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the fifth and last case, a woman who hides her property from her future husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before marrying, a woman may write her property to someone else so her husband won't get it, and she can take it back later. This works only if she wrote away everything. If she kept something for herself, the gift is real and she cannot take it back.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who shelters her property, writing it away so her future husband won't get it

phrases.english: A woman who shelters her property: as the master said:
A woman who shelters her property must write away all of her property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of five sources.
steps.raayaObject: The מברחת case in רב נחמן's list
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching from the master: a מברחת must write away all of her property

steps.title: Keeping movable property counts, except for the כתובה
steps.stepSummary: In all the cases, keeping back only movable property counts as keeping something, except in the כתובה case, because a כתובה is collected only from land.
steps.simpleTranslation: In all these cases, keeping movable property counts as keeping something back, except for the כתובה. רבנן set up the כתובה to be paid from land, not from movable property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the topic by saying what kind of property a person must keep back to avoid the 'all his property' rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, if the giver kept only movable property, that is enough to show he did not give away everything. In the sons case from step 6, where the wife's כתובה is at stake, it is not enough, because a כתובה could only be collected from land. If the husband kept only movable property, there is nothing for her כתובה to be collected from, so she still loses it.

keyTerms.meaning: Movable property, things that can be picked up and carried
The Rabbis set up a rule

steps.whatToRemember: In רב נחמן's five cases, the special rule applies only if the person gave away everything. Keeping movable property counts as keeping something, except for the כתובה, which is paid only from land.
steps.confusionAlert: The exception does not mean the wife wins in the כתובה case. It means keeping only movables does NOT save her, so she still loses her כתובה.

phrases.english: And in all of them, movable property counts as keeping something back,
except for the כתובה,
phrases.notes: He means the sons case from step 6, where the wife loses her כתובה.

phrases.english: since the Rabbis set it up on land,
from movable property the Rabbis did not set it up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After listing all five sources, the גמרא sets one rule about what counts as keeping something back.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Keeping movable property counts as keeping something in all five cases, except the כתובה case, since a כתובה is collected only from land.

steps.title: Movable items written into the marriage contract do count as keeping something
steps.stepSummary: אמימר says that movable items listed in the כתובה, if they still exist, count as a real keeping back of property.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: Movable property that is written in the כתובה and still exists counts as keeping something back.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר adds a limit to the rule from the last step. Usually movable items don't count as keeping something back in the כתובה case, but if they were written into the כתובה and still exist, they do count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8, movable items didn't help the wife because a כתובה is collected only from land. אמימר points out that if the כתובה itself names these movable items as a source of payment, and they still exist, she can collect from them. So keeping them back does leave something for her כתובה, and she does not lose it.

keyTerms.meaning: They still exist in their original form
Keeping back part of the property

steps.whatToRemember: Movable items usually don't count for the כתובה case, but they do if the כתובה names them and they still exist.

phrases.english: Ameimar said:
Movable property that is written in the marriage contract,
and it still exists,
counts as keeping something back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the step 8 rule about the כתובה case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Movable property written in the כתובה that still exists counts as a real keeping back, so the wife does not lose her כתובה.

steps.title: 'My property' includes a slave
steps.stepSummary: A new topic opens: what does 'my property' include? First, a slave, as shown by a משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone said, 'My property goes to so-and-so,' a slave is called 'property,' as we learned in a משנה: One who writes all his property to his slave, the slave goes free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: if a person gives away 'my property,' which things are included? It begins with a slave and proves it from a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a slave who receives 'all his property' goes free. That works only if the slave himself is part of 'property.' He receives himself and so goes free. So the word 'נכסי' includes slaves.

phrases.english: If one said: "My property to so-and-so,"
a slave is called "property,"
as we learned in a משנה:
One who writes all his property to his slave,
phrases.notes: This is the same משנה from step 4.

phrases.english: the slave goes out a free man.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר נִכְסַי לִפְלָנְיָא עַבְדָּא אִיקְּרִי נִכְסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section on what the word 'property' covers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A gift of 'my property' includes slaves.

steps.title: Land and clothing are also called 'property'
steps.stepSummary: Land is 'property' because a משנה calls it 'property with a guarantee,' and a cloak is 'property' because the same משנה calls movable things 'property without a guarantee.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Land is called 'property,' as we learned: Property that has a guarantee is acquired with money, a שטר, or חזקה. A cloak is called 'property,' as we learned: And property that has no guarantee is acquired only by pulling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps building its list. It proves that land and a cloak (movable things) both count as 'property.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in קידושין uses the word 'נכסים' for both land ('with a guarantee') and movable things ('without a guarantee'). Since the משנה uses the word 'property' for both, both are included when someone gives away 'my property.'

keyTerms.meaning: A guarantee. Land can back a debt, so it is 'property with a guarantee'
Taking possession by acting as an owner

phrases.english: Land is called "property,"
as we learned:
Property that has a guarantee
phrases.notes: This means land, because a lender can collect from it.

phrases.english: is acquired with money, with a document, or by taking possession.
A cloak is called "property,"
as we learned:
And property that has no guarantee
is acquired only by pulling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of things called 'property.'
steps.raayaObject: That land and movable items are included in 'my property.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in קידושין that calls both land and movable items 'נכסים.'

steps.title: Money is also called 'property'
steps.stepSummary: Money counts as 'property' because the משנה says movable property can be acquired along with land, and money is acquired that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Money is called 'property,' as we learned: Property without a guarantee can be acquired along with property that has a guarantee, through money, a שטר, or חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds money to the list, again using the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says movable 'property' can be acquired along with land. The גמרא sees money as part of that 'property,' and the next step brings a story that shows money really being acquired this way.

keyTerms.meaning: Acquiring movable things together with land

phrases.english: Money is called "property,"
as we learned:
And property that has no guarantee

phrases.aramaic: נִקְנִין עִם נְכָסִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶן אַחְרָיוּת –
phrases.english: is acquired together with property that has a guarantee
by money, by document, or by taking possession.

steps.raayaObject: That money is included in 'my property.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about acquiring movable property together with land.

steps.title: The story of רב פפא's money
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא transferred money owed to him to רב שמואל בר אחא together with the threshold of his house, showing money can be acquired along with land.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the case of רב פפא, who had twelve thousand זוזים owed to him in בי חוזאי. He transferred them to רב שמואל בר אחא together with the threshold of his house. When he came back, רב פפא went out to meet him as far as תווך.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the last step with a real story. Money was transferred by giving it together with a piece of land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא gave רב שמואל בר אחא a tiny piece of land, the threshold of his house, and 'along with it' the money owed to him far away. This shows in practice that money is the kind of 'property' acquired together with land. רב פפא's going out to greet him shows how grateful he was.

phrases.english: Like this case of Rav Pappa,

phrases.aramaic: הֲווֹ לֵיהּ תְּרֵיסַר אַלְפֵי זוּזֵי בֵּי חוֹזָאֵי,
phrases.english: who had twelve thousand zuz in Bei Ḥozai,

phrases.aramaic: אַקְנִינְהוּ נִיהֲלֵיהּ לְרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אַחָא
phrases.english: he transferred them to Rav Shmuel bar Aḥa
along with the threshold of his house.
When he came back,
he went out to greet him as far as Tavakh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real story that supports step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That money can be acquired together with land.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רב פפא and רב שמואל בר אחא.

steps.title: A document is also called 'property'
steps.stepSummary: A שטר counts as 'property,' shown by רבה בר יצחק's rule that a giver can take back the שטר on its own while the field stays given.
steps.simpleTranslation: A שטר is called 'property,' as רבה בר יצחק said: There are two kinds of documents. If he said, 'Acquire this field for so-and-so, and write him the document,' he can take back the document but not the field. If he said, 'on condition that you write him the document,' he can take back both the document and the field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the list with a שטר (document). It proves this from a rule of רבה בר יצחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case the field is already given, but the giver can still hold back the document. That shows the document is its own item of value, apart from the field. In the second case the gift of the field depends on the document, so he can take back both.
steps.whatToRemember: Slaves, land, movable items, money, and documents are all called 'נכסי,' so a gift of 'my property' includes all of them.
steps.confusionAlert: 'And write' is not the same as 'on condition that you write.' With 'and write,' the field is already given and only the document can be held back. With 'on condition,' the whole gift depends on the document.

phrases.english: A document is called "property,"
as Rabba bar Yitzḥak said:
There are two kinds of documents.
If he said: "Acquire this field for so-and-so,
and write him the document,"
he can take back the document, but he cannot take back the field.
If he said "on condition that you write him the document,"
phrases.notes: The start, 'Acquire this field for so-and-so,' is the same as before and is left out here.

phrases.english: he can take back both the document and the field.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁטָרָא אִיקְּרִי נִכְסֵי דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of things called 'property.'
steps.raayaObject: That a document is included in 'my property.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה בר יצחק's rule that a document can be held back on its own, apart from the field.

steps.title: A third type of deed: the seller wrote it in advance
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says there are three kinds of שטרות. Two are the ones already mentioned, and the third is when the seller wrote the שטר ahead of time. The גמרא starts to point to a משנה about this case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חייא בר אבין said in the name of רב הונא: There are three kinds of deeds. Two are the ones we already said. The other one is when the seller went ahead and wrote the deed first, like the case we learned in a משנה:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second opinion that adds a third kind of שטר to the list. It then opens a quote from a משנה, which is setting up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier teaching listed two kinds of deeds. רב הונא agrees with those two and adds a new case: the seller prepared the deed before the sale happened. The words 'like that which we learned' tell us a משנה about this case is about to be quoted.

keyTerms.meaning: the other one, the remaining one
like that which we learned (a משנה is about to be quoted)

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: And Rav Chiyya bar Avin said that Rav Huna said:
There are three kinds of deeds;
two are the ones that we said,
phrases.notes: These are the two kinds of deeds in the teaching just before this, from step 14.

phrases.english: the other one: if the seller went ahead first
and wrote the deed,
like that case which we learned:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: שְׁלֹשָׁה שְׁטָרוֹת הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the list of deed types from step 14 by adding a third case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are three kinds of שטרות: the two already mentioned, plus the case where the seller wrote the שטר in advance.
